pages.text: Harbourline Freight delivered revenue of 412.6 million pounds in the year ended 31 March 2023, up 9.4% on the prior year. Operating profit was 38.2 million pounds, compared with 31.5 million pounds in 2022. The board recommends a final dividend of 7.5 pence per share. Net debt fell to 96.0 million pounds.

Chair Margaret Oyelaran writes that the group completed the acquisition of Tideway Haulage in September 2022 for 54 million pounds. The company moved its headquarters from Hull to Immingham in January 2023. Headcount at year end was 6,840, an increase of 310 on the previous year. The board met nine times during the year.

Containers handled rose to 1.92 million twenty-foot equivalent units, compared with 1.78 million in 2022. The rail freight division carried 3.4 million tonnes. Average vehicle utilisation improved from 71% to 74%. The fleet comprised 1,215 trucks, of which 188 run on biofuel or electricity.

The Ports division reported revenue of 188.4 million pounds and operating profit of 21.7 million pounds. The Road division reported revenue of 164.9 million pounds and operating profit of 12.3 million pounds. The Rail division reported revenue of 59.3 million pounds and operating profit of 4.2 million pounds.

Carbon emissions were 281,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, down 6% from 2022. The group aims to reach net zero by 2040. The principal risks are fuel price volatility, port labour disputes and cyber attack. A strike at the Teesbank terminal in August 2022 cost an estimated 3.1 million pounds in lost revenue.

Cash generated from operations was 61.8 million pounds. Capital expenditure totalled 47.5 million pounds, mainly new trucks and a rail depot at Doncaster. Basic earnings per share were 21.3 pence. The average interest rate on borrowings was 5.2%. The auditor issued an unqualified opinion on 12 June 2023.

Fernwood Energy generated 5,420 gigawatt hours of electricity in 2023, up from 4,910 in 2022. Revenue was 689 million euros, an increase of 14%. Core profit before tax was 96 million euros. Installed capacity reached 2,150 megawatts.

Chief executive Tomas Lindqvist reports that the Brightwater offshore wind farm began full operation in May 2023 with 380 megawatts of capacity. The company signed a 12-year power purchase agreement with a steel producer for 1.1 terawatt hours a year. Employees numbered 2,310 at year end, 140 more than in 2022. Employee turnover was 8.2%.

Wind accounted for 61% of generation, solar for 27% and hydro for 12%. The average load factor of the wind fleet was 38.5%. Solar capacity grew by 210 megawatts with the Calvera and Ostrow sites. Battery storage capacity stands at 90 megawatt hours.

Net debt was 1.24 billion euros, equal to 3.1 times core earnings. The company issued a 500 million euro green bond in March 2023 with a coupon of 3.75% and a maturity of 2031. Capital expenditure was 740 million euros. The proposed dividend is 0.46 euros per share.

Wholesale power prices averaged 82 euros per megawatt hour, down from 131 in 2022. About 70% of 2024 output is already sold under fixed-price contracts. Weak wind in the third quarter reduced generation by an estimated 160 gigawatt hours. The company reports a lost-time injury rate of 0.9 per million hours worked.

Management expects revenue of 720 to 760 million euros in 2024. Planned investment of 900 million euros includes the 450 megawatt Nordhaven solar park. The company targets 3,000 megawatts of capacity by 2026. It does not give guidance on dividends beyond the current year.

Calder & Moss Retail reported sales of 1.38 billion pounds in the year to 3 February 2024, a rise of 3.2%. Like-for-like sales grew 1.8%. Profit before tax was 74.5 million pounds. Online sales made up 34% of the total.

The group operated 312 stores at year end after opening 14 and closing 21. The average store size is 14,800 square feet. The largest new store opened in Leeds in October 2023 with 42,000 square feet. Customer visits to stores totalled 96 million.
The company employed 18,450 people, of whom 61% worked part time. The starting hourly wage rose to 11.44 pounds in April 2023. Staff turnover was 27%. Training investment was 8.9 million pounds.

Gross margin was 38.6%, down from 39.9% the year before. Own-brand products accounted for 44% of sales. The home and garden category grew 6.1% while clothing fell 2.4%. Stock levels at year end were 212 million pounds.

The company sources from 410 suppliers in 23 countries. About 72% of own-brand products are made in the United Kingdom, Portugal and Turkey. Average delivery time for online orders was 2.3 days. The Daventry distribution centre handled 38 million items.

Net cash at year end was 58.2 million pounds. Capital expenditure was 69 million pounds, with 31 million on store refits. The company paid a dividend of 9.0 pence per share. Free cash flow was 52.4 million pounds.
